1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: rt (well A2 in slot 2)
   line 60:  p20.aspirate(1, block["A2"])
   At line 60 the tip went into rt (well A2 in slot 2) while it still carried buffer (well
   A1 in slot 2), dntp (well A3 in slot 2), primers (well A4 in slot 2), water (well A5 in
   slot 2) and 12 more from an earlier step (this line did it 12 times). A tip that has
   touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now
   holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted
   material along into 11 other wells: wells A2, B1, B2, C1, C2, D1, D2, E1 and 3 more in
   slot 4.
   Affected: well A2 in slot 2.
   Also reached 11 other wells: wells A2, B1, B2, C1, C2, D1, D2, E1 and 3 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 60 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing

   line 45:  p20.aspirate(4, block["A1"])
   At line 45 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5 in slot 2, on a temperature
   module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room temperature until
   `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), dntp (reagent), primers, rt and 1 more
   sat on a block that was never cold; the robot pipetted there 108 times over the run. The
   person setting up the deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3,
   A4 and A5 in slot 2.

   Fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24
   Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 2, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at
   the end.
   Source: Opentrons, temperature module: at room temperature until set_temperature, which
   blocks
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/temperature_module.html

7. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 24 wells of dntp with a sample
   line 52:  p20.dispense(1, well)
   At line 52 the robot starts putting dntp into Bio-Rad 96 Well Plate 200 µL PCR (slot 4),
   and 24 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix
   without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or
   the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can
   tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 16 more in
   slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 16 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 1 ul of dntp and 8 ul of water in place of the
   template, and tell the plate map where it is.

   line 61:  p20.dispense(1, well)

   4, which already held buffer, water, dntp, primers and 12 more (this line did it 12
   times). The addition was 5% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run
   ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so
   what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually
   vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2, D1, D2 and 4 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2, D1, D2 and 4 more in slot 4 after line 61:
   `mix_after=(5, 16)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 16, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
